def: Answering a question by searching a document collection at request time and giving the best passages to a language model in its prompt.
Knowledge stored in a model's weights during training, which cannot be inspected, cited or cheaply corrected.
Knowledge kept outside the model, such as an indexed document collection, that is looked up when a question arrives.
The offline path that parses, chunks, embeds and indexes documents so that they can be searched.
Turning retrieved chunks into one prompt by applying a token budget, removing duplicates, labelling sources and choosing their order.
The fraction of questions for which the chunk holding the supporting evidence is present in the prompt sent to the model.
A short stable tag such as [S1] attached to each chunk in the prompt so the model can cite it and code can map the citation back.
An attack in which instructions hidden in retrieved or fetched content are obeyed by the model as if they came from the user or developer.
A short fingerprint of a chunk's text used to detect whether it changed, so only changed chunks are re-embedded.
Scoring retrieval, assembly, generation and citation separately so that a wrong answer can be traced to the stage that caused it.
